historyTimeline.h2: Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 1.6 EcoBoost was introduced to the Fiesta ST, it replaced the outgoing 1.6T, delivering a significant power increase and establishing the modern ST lineage with its high-revving, turbocharged character and overboost capabilities.

milestones.description: JTJA / JTJB (1.6L Petrol), 182 PS (Launch of the Mk7 Fiesta ST180, featuring a high-output turbocharged EcoBoost unit with a distinctive 3-cylinder soundtrack)
JQJA / JQJB (1.6L Petrol), 200 PS (Introduction of the limited-run Fiesta ST200, featuring an overboost function, uprated internals, and a revised ECU map)
End of 1.6 EcoBoost Production (Replaced by the 1.5 EcoBoost in the Mk7.5 facelift and subsequent Mk8 ST, marking the end of the iconic 1.6 performance era)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost is a highly tunable and robust performance engine, but it suffers from a well-documented design flaw regarding coolant intrusion. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Coolant Intrusion & Head Gasket Failure - Why the Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Overheats
problems.rootCause: The 1.6 EcoBoost block suffers from porosity issues, allowing coolant to seep into the cylinders. This leads to head gasket failure, white exhaust smoke, and eventual engine seizure if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Head gasket replacement, block sealant, and cooling system flush.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable only for early detection with no bore damage or internal contamination.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt unit with updated gaskets and cleared oilways, plus 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if cylinder walls are scored, hydrolock has occurred, or turbo debris has contaminated the block.

problems.recommendation: For isolated head gasket issues caught early, a specialist repair is viable. However, given the block porosity design flaw, a fully rebuilt engine with updated gaskets and cleared oilways is the only reliable long-term solution for a performance vehicle.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Failure & Timing Chain Stretch - High-Output Stress
problems.rootCause: The high boost pressures and thermal cycling can cause turbocharger bearing wear and timing chain tensioner failure, leading to a rattling cold start or catastrophic valve contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Turbocharger replacement or timing chain kit installation with uprated tensioners.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if the core engine block is undamaged and no debris has entered the sump.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full engine replacement, necessary if turbo disintegration or chain skip has sent debris into the engine internals.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if metallic debris has contaminated the engine block or valves are bent.

faq.h2: Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost Engine Replacement - Frequently Asked Questions
faq.intro: Everything Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost owners usually ask before choosing a rebuilt, reconditioned or used replacement engine.

items.question: How much does a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A full rebuilt or reconditioned Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost engine typically costs between £2,500 and £5,000 for the unit itself, depending on the specific engine code and condition.
keyPoints: Fully rebuilt engines with performance warranties cost £3,000 to £5,000.
items.cta: -> Compare Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost engine prices today.

items.question: What are the common signs of Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost engine failure?
items.answer: Owners of the Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost often report specific warning signs before total failure, primarily linked to the cooling system and block porosity.
keyPoints: Unexplained coolant loss without visible external leaks, often accompanied by white smoke from the exhaust.
A rattling or knocking noise from the engine on cold startup, indicating potential timing chain tensioner wear.
items.cta: -> Get a diagnostic quote from a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost specialist.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost?
items.answer: Yes, absolutely. The Mk7 Fiesta ST holds strong residual values, typically ranging from £8,000 to £16,000 depending on condition and edition.
keyPoints: A £3,000-£4,500 rebuilt engine represents a fraction of the vehicle's total value.
Replacing the engine preserves the car's performance and resale value far better than selling a non-running example at a steep discount.
items.cta: -> Check if your Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost is a candidate for replacement.

items.question: What is the difference between the JTJA and JQJA Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost engines?
items.answer: Both are 1.6L turbocharged petrol engines, but they serve different performance tiers within the ST lineup.
keyPoints: JTJA / JTJB produces 182 PS and is fitted to the standard Fiesta ST180.
JQJA / JQJB produces 200 PS and is fitted to the limited-run Fiesta ST200, featuring an overboost function and uprated internals.
items.cta: -> Confirm your exact Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost engine code by entering your registration.

items.question: How long does a Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost engine replacement take?
items.answer: A standard Ford Fiesta ST 1.6 EcoBoost engine swap typically takes 1 to 2 days of labour once the replacement unit has arrived.
keyPoints: Sourcing and delivering the engine usually takes 2-4 working days.
Total turnaround from quote to completion is generally 5-7 working days.
